newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, FEB 17-SUNDAY, FEB 23 (PAGE 1/3 - MONDAY) - REUTER EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, FEB 17-SUNDAY, FEB 23 (PAGE 1/3 - MONDAY) - REUTER EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
BRUSSELS - EU finance ministers meet (Monday); main discussions focus on economic situation in the EU.
BRUSSELS - EU agricultural ministers meet (Monday-Tuesday); main discussions focus on identification of cattle and beef labelling.

STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (Monday-Friday); vote on report by the committee of inquiry on handling of the mad cow disease crisis - followed by a news conference (Wednesday).
DOHA, Qatar - Ministerial meeting and seventh joint council between the Gulf Cooperation Council and the EU (Monday); Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo and European Commissioner Marin attend.

BRUSSELS - U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright meets European Commission President Santer, Commisioners Brittan, de Silguy, Bonino and van den Broek - followed by a joint news conference with Santer and Brittan (Tuesday).
BRUSSELS - North Atlantic Council holds informal discussions of key issues facing NATO, particularly the internal and external adaptation of the alliance, including NATO-Russia relations (Tuesday).
BRUSSELS - NATO Secretary General Javier Solana meets Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov (Sunday); discussions focus on a permanent consultative mechanism between Moscow and the alliance.
MONDAY, FEBRUARY 17
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - ECOFIN Council (1000/0900 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- Convergence programme for Belgium.
- Financial assistance to third countries:
- Commission proposal for Armenia, Georgia and Tajikistan;
- Commission information on Former Yugoslavian Republic of Madedonia.
- Economic situation in the EU.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Farm Council (1500/1400 GMT) (and Tuesday).
Agenda includes:
- Commission report on the tobacco market - orientation debate.
- (possibly) Commission presentation of report on the reform of the common organisation of the olive oil market.
- Identification of cattle and beef labelling - discussion and proposal.
- Proposal for regulation on member states' action programme on control of expenses under EAGGF, guarantee section.
- (possibly) Proposal modifying the regulation of geographical identification of origin in farm products and foodstuffs.
- Commission report to the Council, at Portuguese request, following the EU-U.S. Blair House agreement report on oil seeds.
- Future of WTO in milk and dairy products:
- Italian delegation reflection document;
- British delegation document.
- Commission oral report on the state of work in the negotiations with third countries for the conclusion of veterinary and plant health equivalency agreements.
STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (to Friday).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (1700/1600 GMT) Announcement of motion to censure the European Commission in relation to the mad cow disease crisis.
- Report on the conclusion by the EC of the Energy Charter Treaty and the protocol on energy efficiency and related environmental aspects.
- Guido Podesta report on development problems and structural interventions in Italy.
- Gerhard Botz report on development problems and structural interventions in Germany for 1994-1999.
- Konstantinos Hatzidakis report on Commission communication on cohesion and environment policy.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1900/1800 GMT) Foreign Affairs;
Economic;
Legal Affairs;
Environment.

AMSTERDAM - Dutch EU presidency hosts experts meeting on public service broadcasting in Europe (and Tuesday). Main discussions focus on the role of public service broadcasting in the information society; public financing of public service broadcasting in relation to the treaty and EC competition policy; international cooperation between public service broadcasters. Venue: Grand Hotel Krasnapolsky. Contact: Andre Matthijse, Netherlands Broadcasting Corporation NOS (31) 35 677 37 87.

DOHA, Qatar - Ministerial meeting and seventh joint council between the Gulf Cooperation Council and the EU. Discussions focus on the implementation of the cooperation agreement; free trade agreement negotiations; exchange of views on development in the two regions; exchange of views on political questions of common interest and approval of the joint declaration - followed by a closing news conference. Participants include: Qatar Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad Bin Jaber Al-Thani, Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo and European Commissioner Marin.
TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 18

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright meets European Commission President Santer, Commissioners Brittan, de Silguy, Bonino and van den Broek (0930/0830 GMT) - followed by a joint news conference with Santer and Brittan (1020/0920 GMT).
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (second of five days).
Provisional agenda includes:

- (0900/0800 GMT) Ria Oomen-Ruijten report on the application of social security regimes to employees and their family members who move in the Community; Oomen-Ruijten recommendation on consumer protection in unit pricing.
- Barbara Weiler report on social protection in Europe and on the future of social protection.
- (1200/1100 GMT) Final vote on report by Giacomo Santini on bananas.

- (NEW ITEM) (1500/1400 GMT) Manuel Medina Ortega report on allegations of infringement or bad administration on the application of Community law on BSE (mad cow disease); European Commission President Santer gives address.
- (2100/2000 GMT) Questions to the Commission.
- (2200/2100 GMT) Gianni Tamino recommendation on state aids for transport.
- James Janssen van Raay report on investor compensation schemes.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1730/1630 GMT) Energy;
Employment;
Youth;
Institutional Affairs.
STRASBOURG - EP Union for Europe holds press lunch (1300/1200 GMT). Venue: 76, Allee de la Robertsau. Contact: Union for Europe (33) 3 88 17 46 36.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - North Atlantic Council holds informal discussions of key issues facing NATO, particularly the internal and external adaptation of the Alliance, including NATO-Russia relations (1430/1330 GMT). U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright attends. NATO Secretary General Javier Solana holds news conference at 1715/1615 GMT.

AMSTERDAM - Dutch EU presidency hosts experts meeting on public service broadcasting in Europe (second of two days). News conference on the outcome of the meeting at 1300/1200 GMT. Venue: Grand Hotel Krasnapolsky. Contact: Andre Matthijse, Netherlands Broadcasting Corporation NOS (31) 35 677 37 87.
WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 19
STRASBURG (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (0900/0800 GMT).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Commissioner Monti communication on refund of import duties.
- Commissioner Marin communication on the state of play on Euro-Mediterranean partnership accord and preparation for the second ministerial conference.

- European Commission President Santer and Commissioners Brittan, Marin, van den Broek, de deus Pinheiro, Bonino and Liikanen joint communication on EU special envoys in the framework of foreign policy in security.
- Commissioner Wulf-Mathies communication on objective 2 for Italy, Germany and Denmark (1997-1998); modification of programming document for objective 5 for Luxembourg (1994-1999).
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (third of five days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (0900/0800 GMT) Mihail Papayannakis report on labelling of beef and beef-based products.
- Karl Erik Olsson report on the organisation of veterinary control on products from third countries entering the Community.
- Xaver Mayer report on beef identification and registration system.
- Ken Collins report on pharmaceuticals in animal feed.
- Philip Whitehead report on priorities for consumer policy.
- Elena Marinucci report on financial services: responding to consumer expectations.
- Marlies Mosiek-Urbahn report on the laws of the member states on consumer credit.
- Ernesto Caccavale report on consumer credit.
- Evelyne Gebhardt report on recognition of diplomas.
- Malou Lindholm report on equal treatment of men and women: amendment of the staff regulations of officials of the European Communities.
- (1200/1100 GMT) Votes on:
- Motions for resolutions on which the debate is closed, including the report on BSE.
- (NEW ITEM) (1330/1230 GMT) Manuel Medina Ortega holds news conference on the report on the handling of the BSE crisis.
- (1630/1530 GMT) Council statement on EU policy towards Algeria.
- (1730/1630 GMT) Questions to the Council.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1700/1600 GMT) Budget.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Eurogroup for animal welfare holds news conference on "No retrieve for leghold traps - Time to respect regulation 3254/91" at 1000/0900 GMT. Venue: IPE3 press room.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds conference on "Post-Papandreou Greece: new economic and foreign policy directions" (0900/0800 GMT). Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.

LONDON - Agra Europe holds 16th annual European outlook '97 conference (0830/0830 GMT) (and Thursday). Speakers include: British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg. Venue: The Landmark Hotel. Contact: Agra Europe (44) 1892 511 807.
THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 20
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (fourth of five days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (1000/0900 GMT) Imelda Read report on the application of an open network to voice telephony and the establishment of a universal telecoms service in a competitive environment.
- W.G. van Velzen report on telecommunications and Open Network Provision.
- Karsten Hoppenstedt report on satellite communications.
- (1200/1100 GMT) Votes on reports under cooperation, codecision and assent procedures and on other motions for resolutions on which debate has closed.
- (1500/1400 GMT) Vote on motion to censure the European Commission for its handling of the BSE crisis.
- Debates on topical and urgent subjects of major importance - followed by votes.
- (1800/1700 GMT) Monica Stefania Baldi report on EU-ACP Joint Assembly in 1996.
- Michael McGowan report on complementarity between the EU's cooperation and development policy and those of member states.
- Raimondo Fassa report on links between emergency aid, rehabilitation and development.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - EP deputies John Tomlinson and Edward Kellett-Bowman hold news conference on the report on the EU's transit system (1000/0900 GMT).
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz meets WEU Secretary General Jose Cutileiro.
FRIDAY, FEBRUARY 21
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Santer addresses "Transatlantic relations" conference.
STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (last of five days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Votes on procedures without report; votes on reports without debate; motions for resolutions on which debate has closed.
- Jan Mulder report on balancing of member state accounts on expenses financed by EAGGF, guarantee section, for 1992 as well as certain expenses for 1993.
- Astrid Lulling report on spouses helping independent workers.
- Oral question on leghold traps.
- Oral question on genetic maize.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - NATO Secretary General Javier Solana meets Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz (0900/0800 GMT).
SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 22

LOUVAIN-LA-NEUVE - Leuven Catholic University (UCL) European Studies Institute holds conference on "European policy in Belgium" (0900/0800 GMT). Venue: UCL, Urbain Vaes Hall. Contact: European Studies Institute (3210) 47 85 50.
SUNDAY, FEBRUARY 23
BRUSSELS - NATO Secretary General Javier Solana meets Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov. The talks will centre on a permanent consultative mechanism between Moscow and the alliance.
